newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 4.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Nelson Mandela met new United Nations (UN) Secretary General Kofi Annan, and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, during his Swiss trip, and was hoping to meet a senior government representative from the People's Republic of China, presidential spokesman Parks Mankahlana said.

- Sun International South Africa Ltd is in advanced negotiations to sell or close eight of its seventeen casino resorts by the end of this year, two years ahead of the deadline set by government for the group to rationalise its operations.

- Mining group JCI Ltd has signed a letter of intent to acquire Shell Southern Africa's coal business in a transaction which will put the group into the top flight of South African coal producers and which endorses its pledge to expand its mining operations across the board.
- Foreigners have been piling into South Africa's gilts market this year, helping the rand firm about 14c against a strong US dollar.

- Carson Holdings Ltd, the local hair care and beauty cosmetics manufacturer, is expected to more than double its size when it acquires Black Like Me Products, Carson Inc, Carson's US parent company, said last week,.
- Cheap textiles flooding the Durban market might have been stolen from government warehouses, textile brokers said yesterday.

- A 400 million rand contract to supply Cuba with 10 000 truck engines will boost Cape-based Atlantis Diesel Engines' turnover by 35 percent to about 1 billion rand a year, but could lead to a further deterioration in US-South African relations, international affairs commentators said yesterday.
- The Johannesburg Stock Exchange yesterday announced that an official options market for shares will be launched in October.
- Shoredits Holdings Ltd SHOJn J, a construction company registered at the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, has been provisionally liquidated.
- A massive cleanup of the police force to beef up its flagging performance against crime was announced by Police Commissioner George Fivaz in Pretoria yesterday.
- A Supreme Court judge who was hijacked in Johannesburg, has attributed the high number of hijackings in Glenhazel suburb to the "total ineffectiveness of police services in the area".
